title: Successive quotient normalizations under the pulled reduction comparison
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and use the adic datum, small pro-etale sites and coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $W=T,T'$ put $B_W=A_W$, $R_W=\underline A_W$ and $S_{n,W}=(P_n)_W$. Let $K\in D(B_T)$ be arbitrary, $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{n,T}$, $N=Lg_R^*\operatorname{Res}_T K$, $N_n=N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$, and $H_n=Lg_n^*K_n$. Use finite module pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and the specified finite coefficient isomorphisms $\tau_n:N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison].

For $b\geq a\geq1$ let $\theta^N_{b,a}:N_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\to N_a$ be successive scalar-extension normalization [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Define $\theta^H_{b,a}:H_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\to H_a$ by the canonical pullback/scalar-extension comparison followed by $Lg_a^*$ of the normalization $K_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T}\to K_a$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Then $\theta^H_{b,a}$ is invertible and
$$\theta^H_{b,a}\circ(\tau_b\otimes^L1)=\tau_a\circ\theta^N_{b,a}.$$
The comparisons are natural in $K$. For $c\geq b\geq a$, successive $\theta^H_{c,b}$ and $\theta^H_{b,a}$ equal $\theta^H_{c,a}$ under canonical derived scalar associativity; for $b=a$ the map $\theta^H_{a,a}$ is the scalar-extension unit identification.

On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], these are the derived maps induced by the balancing maps $(x\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$ before and after inverse image and scalar extension. The two triple-normalization composites are the map $((x\otimes t)\otimes s)\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$ under the same comparisons. These formulas specify morphisms of sheaf tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the stated comparisons and equalities hold independently of the chosen K-flat representative.

proof.text: Choose normalized scalar adjunctions for the fixed published scalar presentations. Use the ordinary and derived composition API of successive quotient normalization. Its ordinary generator formula identifies the induced cochain compositor with reductionBalance; no large normalization witness is unfolded in this identification. Transport equality of coefficient maps on the whole scalar isomorphism before whiskering, rather than composing with an equality isomorphism of chosen derived functors. Proved legacy equalities certify that thetaN and quotientAssociator retain exactly their original values.

proof.text: Completed coefficient flatness makes restriction of a flat-term K-flat completed-coefficient complex K-flat over the constant ring with flat terms. Ringed inverse image preserves these two properties. The published scalar and exact pullback counits are therefore invertible on the chosen representatives.

proof.text: The constant finite quotient is sectionwise surjective: transport the constant quotient through the specified finite coefficient identification and use the constant-completion quotient computation. Restriction along this quotient is fully faithful. Cancel restriction in OrderedExchange.ordinaryRho to obtain the ordinary coefficient comparison; its tensor formula is the defining formula of ordinaryRho.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized scalar cochain transpose from the sheaf-ring derived Hom comparison and the homotopy-to-cochain compatibility theorem. Uniqueness identifies this adjunction with the published scalar adjunction. The exact restriction/pullback square and the derived mate comparison then compute the canonical pullback/scalar mate on every cochain representative. Normalized adjunction uniqueness also gives the scalar identity representative.

proof.text: Compose the ordinary coefficient comparison with the ordinary inverse-image/scalar mate to define ordinaryTau. The unit formulas determine its value on the tensor generators of the strict comparison. Compose the finite ordinary mate with ordinary scalar collapse to define ordinaryTheta. On generators it sends a finite pullback generator times t, tensored with s, to that generator times q(t)s. These formulas prove the ordinary square, the two displayed triple formulas, and the scalar identity formula.

proof.text: Flat-term K-flat resolutions exist on the original site. Apply the existing comparison-on-resolutions construction to ordinaryTau and the invertible computation counits. It yields a natural derived isomorphism tau with precisely the required representative equation. This construction does not require completeness of the input derived object.

proof.text: Use the scalar-collapse and derived-mate representative equations to compute thetaH and thetaN on the same resolutions. The ordinary square and naturality of the counits prove the derived square there; equality of natural transformations is detected on the resolving class, so the square holds everywhere. Transport scalar associativity through this square to prove the thetaH cocycle. Apply the identity representative and the ordinary unit calculation in the same way to prove the unit equation. This establishes all fields of Comparison, including naturality and independence of representatives.
